summary: Implemented the owner's Android tooling cleanup. tools/android now contains only native Rust preparation, build-only packaging and read-only device preflight; custom OCR/frame/edit/reopen drivers, fixture orchestration and their dead dependencies are removed. Android owns the existing Rust JNI Keystore implementation and encrypted-record code directly, with no production dependency on operator tooling. Deleted the obsolete Java session helper and all remaining Android/scripts PowerShell helpers. Android documentation names Rust commands. The offline JSON fixture remains because the application still consumes it. Core launch, browse, login, session resolution and logout behavior were not redesigned. No substitute UI automation, commits or pushes were added.
evidence: cargo update --offline --manifest-path tools/android/Cargo.toml --workspace and cargo update --offline --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml --workspace passed. Lockfiles were pruned without upgrading retained packages. Removed direct tooling dependencies include Windows OCR, regex, URL/UUID, randomness and JNI; legitimate transitive platform dependencies were retained.
cargo fmt --manifest-path tools/android/Cargo.toml -- --check and cargo fmt --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml -- --check passed after rustfmt.

cargo test --locked --manifest-path tools/android/Cargo.toml passed: 6 tests, zero failures/ignored/filtered. Covers unsafe adb configuration, wrong AVD/boot/ABI, malformed or mismatched server rejection before device commands, output preservation, preparation checksum rejection and failed/hung child cleanup.

cargo test --locked --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml passed: 3 encrypted-record integration tests, zero failures/ignored/filtered. Exercises the production file module: exact legacy bytes/path/AAD, reopen reads, atomic replacement, origin isolation, corrupt-record preservation, invalid cipher-output rejection and selected-origin/pending-write cleanup. These are non-UI persistence tests, not cryptographic platform tests.

cargo clippy --locked --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo clippy --locked --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml --target x86_64-linux-android --lib -- -D warnings passed. The latter compiled the actual Android shell and checked JNI Keystore calls after relocation, not the empty host shell. Platform storage retains the AES-256 key alias, Keystore-chosen IV, AES-GCM tag, version-1 72-byte record and exact-origin authentication used by the deleted Java helper.

cargo run --locked --manifest-path tools/android/Cargo.toml -- prepare-mobile passed against the prepared source. cargo run --locked --manifest-path tools/android/Cargo.toml -- test-prepare-mobile passed all six isolated public-source preparation/tamper/cleanup scenarios. The invalid-patch scenario emitted its expected Git error and confirmed cleanup.

cargo run --locked --manifest-path tools/android/Cargo.toml -- --help exposed only prepare-mobile, test-prepare-mobile, build-debug, check-device and help. Running each of frame, edit, reopen and ocr-frame through that same Cargo command rejected it with parser exit 2. check-device with absent device configuration failed closed with exit 1 before contacting adb.

cargo tree --locked --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml --target x86_64-linux-android --edges normal --prefix none --format '{p}' passed; assertions found no boardcraft-android-tools, tempfile or clap in the production graph. Filesystem checks confirmed all retired Rust driver modules, displaced session modules, Java helper and five PowerShell helpers are absent. No authored PowerShell remains under android/scripts outside prepared upstream sources. android/src/lib.rs still calls scripts/fixtures/android-kit-board.json, so deleting that fixture would break the offline shell.

git diff --check -- android scripts tools/android passed. Edits were limited to android, tools/android, the explicitly authorized scripts/dev.ps1 and scripts/postgres.ps1 deletions, and this handoff. Root Cargo files, web, tools/src, runner gates, verification markers and other workers' documentation/handoffs were not edited by this task. Shared legacy links/gates were left for their owners rather than changing those files.
